pistons.body:
DETROIT, MI - APRIL 8: Daniss Jenkins #24 of the Detroit Pistons dribbles the ball during the game against the Milwaukee Bucks on April 8, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

An undermanned (due to injury) Detroit Pistons team will be taking on an undermanned (due to rebuilding) Milwaukee Bucks team today at Little Caesars Arena. A win will essentially seal Detroit’s win in East Group A of the NBA Cup. The best any team can finish, including Detroit is 3-1 overall, and Detroit has the tiebreaker against the Orlando Magic. Detroit’s 29-point differential also easily eclipses the next closest team, Toronto, which stands at just plus-9. The winner of each group advances to the knockout round.

Game Vitals

When: 7:30 p.m. ET
Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, Michigan
Watch: TV: TV20 Detroit | Streaming: DAZN-Det
Odds: Pistons -10.5

Analysis

In the way are the Bucks, and look, we all remember what the Pistons were like once they cleared the books of Reggie Jackson, Andre Drummond, and Blake Griffin. It was a bit of a hodgepodge mess. Milwaukee is currently in its hodgepodge era. They have the worst record in the NBA, winning just two of their 19 games. They have a bottom-five offense, a bottom-five defense, and the second-worst net rating in the NBA behind the Kings. They are one of the worst-shooting teams in the NBA becaue they don’t really have pieces that fit together. They have some talent — I like Ryan Rollins and Jaime Jaquez, and Tyler Herro is an exceptionally dangerous offensive force. But they are a team currently better than the sum of their parts. And that probably isn’t changing at any point this season.

But Detroit has issues of its own entering tonight. Namely, they will be down three starters, including superstar Cade Cunningham. Cade has been nursing a sore knee, and the Pistons are understandably taking zero chances. They will also be down Jalen Duren, who is close to a return, and Duncan Robinson, likewise.

The Pistons were also without all three starters in their most recent game, and still easily dispatched the Orlando Magic 104-86 because Detroit locked in defensively and got plenty of quality minutes from Ausar Thompson and Daniss Jenkins. Isaiah Joe also had the best game of his brief tenure with the Pistons, leading Detroit with 21 points and looking comfortable knocking down 3-pointers.

Detroit can muddle through the season without Cade; they showed it last season, too. They truly need to do whatever is needed to ensure this knee issue doesn’t linger and he is helpful for what we hope is a deep playoff run.

Projected Starters

Detroit Pistons (11-6)

Daniss Jenkins, Isaiah Joe, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

Milwaukee Bucks (2-17)

Ryan Rollins, Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez, Kyle Kuzma, Myles Turner

Question of the Game

If you could trade for one member of the Milwaukee Bucks, who would it be?

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Magic final score: Detroit’s dominant defense shows up with Cade Cunningham sidelined
pistons.body:
ORLANDO, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 24: Isaiah Joe #17 of the Detroit Pistons reacts after scoring a three-pointer against the Orlando Magic during the fourth quarter of a Emirates NBA Cup game at Kia Center on November 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Goin to Work Pistons showed up tonight. Detroit dispatched the Orlando Magic 104-86. This was another statement game. It doesn’t matter who plays; defense travels. Detroit is now 2-1 in NBA Cup play with a plus-31 point differential. Orlando felt Detroit’s defensive wrath, holding Orlando to 14 second-quarter points. They were everywhere.

Cade Cunningham was a late scratch, but the next man steps up here. Both teams struggled to put the ball in the hoop, but Detroit generated better shots. They swung the ball from side to side on plenty of possessions. The shot-making results weren’t always there, but their process was solid. It was probably more than solid considering they were down three starters tonight.

Ausar Thompson and Daniss Jenkins picked up more on-ball reps. Jenkins had a 15-point and 10-assist double-double. Thompson continues to grow as a playmaker for others as he added seven more assists tonight.

Ausar seems much more sure of himself this season. Even the moments he turns down shots to find a teammate are telling — everything seems planned.

Ausar wasn’t the only Piston with an all-around A performance. Kevin Huerter finished with 13-5-6. He worked the off-ball screen here, slightly froze the big, and threw an accurate lob to Paul Reed.

The OOP 🎯 pic.twitter.com/VetSoIuf8f
— Detroit Pistons (@DetroitPistons) November 25, 2026

Isaiah Joe led the team with 21 points. He went 5-for-11 from trey. Joe showed off the range and confidence. He pressured the ball on the other end. Shooters competing on defense, and not being must-hide defenders, is such a plus. Joe is picking it up.

Ron Holland has success from deep. He buried two 3s. Detroit shot it well as a team despite their low point total. They went 15-for-36 from deep compared to Orlando’s 12-for-36. John Collins, Woo, and Elijah Harkless (he made some momentum-swinging ones) all hit two 3s.

Detroit knocked down 3s but kept Orlando from doing anything. Franz Wagner had been on a hot streak until he ran into this defense (29 PPG over the last 10). He (20 pts) and Desmond Bane (21 pts) put numbers on the board, but it wasn’t easy. Those two saw a crowd every time they drove the ball. Wagner started spamming push shots that felt automatic, but Detroit held him in check.

Anthony Black was a non-factor offensively tonight. That’s a testament to Detroit’s D, as he’s been rolling all year. The Magic missed so many shots at the rim. They were initially dominating Detroit on the offensive glass, but those missed shots eventually turned into Detroit run-outs.

The Pistons also got their hands on so many Magic passes tonight. They made Orlando creators play with multiple hands in their faces and trusted their closeouts to disrupt “open” Orlando 3s. Holding a team under 90 in 2026 is some Goin to Work stuff. Hats off to J.B. Bickerstaff for having this defense ready to go at all times.

Detroit’s final group play cup game is Friday versus the flaming hot Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks. Detroit could still win the group even after losing to the Toronto Raptors last Friday. They might need some help, but must start by handling their business with the Bucks.

pistons.headline: Pistons at Hawks final score: Detroit outscored by 21 in the fourth, lose 107-97
pistons.body:
ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 22: Nickeil Alexander-Walker #7 of the Atlanta Hawks reacts after hitting a three-point basket against the Detroit Pistons during the first quarter at State Farm Arena on November 22, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images

That was an unbelievable collapse by Detroit, and quite possibly the worst game of Cade Cunningham’s career.

The Pistons went into the fourth quarter with an 85-74 lead. They outscored the Hawks by 10 in the third quarter, and ESPN had Detroit at a 90% chance to win the game when the final frame started.

That went downhill quickly as the Hawks went on an 18-0 run to open the fourth quarter. The Pistons didn’t score their first points until Isaiah Joe hit a corner three with 4:52 left in the game. Detroit’s offense stalled, the ball wasn’t moving, and for whatever reason, Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins took it upon themselves to try to iso Dyson Daniels and Lu Dort. As you can tell, it didn’t work.

Detroit shot better from the field, the three-point line, and the free-throw line. They even scored more points in the paint than the Hawks, but couldn’t manage to grab a rebound. Atlanta grabbed 19 more rebounds than Detroit and outrebounded the Pistons on the offensive glass 24-8. If there was ever a game that showed Detroit needed Jalen Duren back ASAP, this was it.

Atlanta had 10 more fastbreak points than Detroit, and second-chance points went in a massive favor of the Hawks to the tune of 27-6. Detroit’s rebounding was horrendous – outside of Ausar Thompson’s 11 boards, John Collins was second on the team with six.

Cade Cunningham scored in single digits for the first time all season with five points while shooting 2-for-9 from the field. He also added four rebounds and 15 assists in what is surely one of the weirdest stat lines of his career. Kevin Huerter was a -28 on the floor while shooting 1-for-8 for a measly two points.

Oddly enough, it was Isaiah Joe who led the team in scoring with 19 points on 15 attempts. Joe was +11 tonight and knocked down three threes. John Collins and Ausar Thompson each had 18 points. Collins made four threes, and Ausar added five assists. Paul Reed had 16 points off the bench, and Daniss Jenkins had 11.

In what should’ve been a victory tonight in Atlanta, Detroit blew their double-digit lead and deserved to lose this game. That was one of the worst fourth quarter performances I’ve ever watched, and it looked like a middle school team that couldn’t grab a rebound in a scrimmage against the high school varsity.

Please, Jalen Duren, come back soon.

Detroit moves to 10-6 on the year and will now travel to Orlando to take on the Magic on Tuesday night. Let’s hope this Pistons team has a short memory and burns tonight’s fourth quarter tape.

Go Stones.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Raptors final score: Cade vs. Scottie battle goes to Raps
pistons.body:
[DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 20: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons plays defense on Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Two former teammates and two Eastern Conference teams traded body blows all night. A Cade Cunningham 3-pointer to put the Pistons up 102-101 with 20 seconds left was answered by a Scottie Barnes driving layup over two defenders to give the Raptors the lead they would not relinquish. When a Kevin Huerter three came up short as the buzzer sounded, it was decided. Raptors 105-102.

Cunningham led Detroit with 23 points and nine assists, but he was outshined on this night by his former Montverde teammate Barnes, who led all scorers with 29 points and hit his first nine shots of the night.

While it was appointment television watching the two top players on each team matched up with each other, the rest of the game was pretty much a horror show for the Pistons. Distilling why the Pistons dropped this game will sound very familiar to Pistons fans — not owning the paint.

Detroit surrendered 54 points inside to Toronto and gave up crucial offensive rebounds late. It’s one thing to see Barnes put a great game on you, but Detroit was owned inside by rookie Allen Graves making his first start of the season. He scored 20 points, had 10 rebounds, including four on the offensive end. Detroit simply had no answer for him. Certainly not John Collins.

The overmatched emergency starting center struggled again in just under 20 minutes of action. He was just 1-of-4 from the floor for three points and six rebounds. The return of Isaiah Joe from injury isn’t looking very different from when he was playing early in the season — he’s still struggling to find his shot. Joe was 1-of-6 from deep tonight. Getting those kinds of performances from your two highest-profile offseason acquisitions is not the recipe for winning basketball.

The other major issue tonight is that you were facing one of the worst-shooting offenses in the NBA and on this night, they could not miss. Some of that had to do with Detroit’s occasionally passive defense. But tonight, the Raptors players were just collectively on one. We already covered how hot Barnes was, especially early, but the sweet shooting was up and down the roster.

The rookie Graves was 6-of-9, Jakob Poeltl was 5-of-7, and Immanuel Quickly was 6-of-10. Collectively, Toronto shot 67% inside the arc tonight. Again, I’m going to point to the big black hole in the middle of Detroit’s lineup. A combination of John Collins and Paul Reed as your only big men is just not going to get it done in the NBA. The Pistons need Jalen Duren to come back desperately.

The loss to the Raptors drops the Pistons to 1-1 in NBA Cup play, but then again, I refuse to care about the NBA Cup. Detroit now goes on a mini road trip to Atlanta on Sunday and Orlando on Tuesday before enjoying seven of the next eight games at home.

The Toronto Raptors are scuffling in the first leg of the NBA season, but there is certainly a lot of talent there. Yes, Kawhi Leonard is absent with news of managing knee pain and swelling that surely puts a shiver up the spine of every Toronto fan. But they also still have Scottie Barnes, and he is delivering the young star goods as advertised. He is averaging 23.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 4.7 assists a night. On certain nights, he looks like the young superstar that represents his clearly attainable ceiling. On other nights, he and his team’s offense struggle and can’t seem to get unstuck from the mud. He’s doing a lot of things, but he isn’t doing it as efficiently or consistently as you’d like.

The real problems with the Raptors, though, lie elsewhere. Nobody can seemingly hit a three. RJ Barrett is getting to the line five times a game and hitting just 60% from the charity stripe. Collin Murray-Boyles has regressed, and Jakob Poeltl’s game has fallen off a cliff. It feels like if you solve Scottie, it helps you solve Barrett and Immanuel Quickley, and therefore, you solve the Raptors. Toronto has dropped six straight, and will be without the services of Barrett tonight.

Watching an Ausar Thompson and Scottie Barnes matchup could be electric. Barnes doesn’t have the defensive chops Ausar does, and Ausar doesn’t have the offensive versatility, but both could be liable to pull off a triple-double tonight. Cade Cunningham is also expected back tonight after sitting out Detroit’s win against the New Orleans Pelicans. Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland are out, and doubtful, respectively.

pistons.body:
DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 16: Isaiah Joe #17 of the Detroit Pistons shoots the ball during the game against the Toronto Raptors on October 16, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Early season Fridays = NBA Cup day! The Detroit Pistons can climb to 2-0 in group play with a win over the worse-than-expected Toronto Raptors (1-1 in group play). The NBA thought this would’ve been a big game, handing out the Prime Video first game slot, but injuries, injuries, injuries.

Ron Holland, Duncan Robinson, and Jalen Duren are out again, but Cade Cunningham is expected to play. Injuries have slowed down the Raptors a ton.

RJ Barrett and Collin Murray-Boyles won’t suit up in Detroit. Kawhi Leonard remains out. His absence is the main source of Toronto’s struggle, but I still expected more.

GAME VITALS

Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MI

When: 7:30 PM ET

Watch: Prime Video

Odds: Pistons (-6.5)

The Raptors are still live even though they should be better. That said, Detroit isn’t a team that takes opponents lightly because of who’s in or out. The Pistons play the same brand of ball regardless of who’s out there on either side.

Wednesday’s 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans tripled down on that point. Even a shorthanded Pistons squad without Cade manages to find a way.

Daniss Jenkins. Javonte Green. Ausar Thompson with the ball. Paul Reed with extended minutes — trustworthy things.

We got Isaiah Joe back in the lineup in that one! One of the marquee signings of Detroit’s offseason let it fly. Joe went 3-for-5 from range and put it on the floor, aiding Detroit’s flow. Bball Paul said Joe had more in his game during media day. Paul knows ball.

What do you know, it's Isaiah Joe

-Pistons able to flow into early offense with nothing there on initial push. DHO and now Joe gets a flare with an empty side
-Huerter cuts backdoor, pindown for Joe with an empty side. Turns the corner and the lob is there. pic.twitter.com/LZ8FQlRRAH
— Steve Jones (@stevejones20) November 19, 2026

The ability to leverage your shooting with live dribble decisions is an invaluable skill come playoff time. Love seeing Joe back out there, and more of that would be cool.

John Collins was on a heater (4-6 on 3s). He should get six 3s up every night with the room he has to fire. Collins will be matched up with Jakob Poeltl tonight. Poeltl is arguably the biggest hacker in the league. His 5.6 foul percentage ranks in the fourth percentile among bigs.

A lot of those Cade drives should end with trips to the charity stripe. Cade’s .37 FTr is a career high. He’s getting the calls and shooting ~86 percent at the line. That works. Cade is also putting together a strong All-Defense case, being a big-time contributor on the sixth-best defense.

Per Stathead, only Cade, Nikola Jokić, Matisse Thybulle, Scottie Barnes, and Caleb Wilson are averaging at least 0.9 blocks and 1.4 steals. Cade is doing this without fouling. He’s leveling up even more on that end.

Barnes recently declared himself the best defender in the world. I have no problem with that. He is up there. He’s a legit 1-5 defender. Anybody that good at something should feel they’re the best. That confidence got them where they are.

Barnes is Barnes, but I thought Toronto would have a more intimidating team defense. Cleaning The Glass ranks them 17th overall and 19th over the past two weeks + they are on a six-game losing streak.

The injury bug cannot be ignored, but I thought Toronto would be immune to long stretches of defensive lapses because of their suffocating gap principles.

Those principles still force turnovers at a frightening rate (2nd), but they haven’t dug in and clamped down like last year’s Raptors team. They’re still feisty enough to muddy up a game, but I expected more.

Toronto’s off-the-bounce creation takes a big blow with no Kawhi and Barrett. Barnes has more shot-making responsibilities this season. His 23.8 points per game are a career high. Immanuel Quickley will get them up. Catching fire vs. Ausar and the Pistons’ defense isn’t easy, but Toronto is looking to Quickley to provide immediate offense.

Jamison Battle is one of Toronto’s consistent snipers. He’s not a shooter you can disregard and is coming off a 19-point, 5-for-10 from 3 game. Ja’Kobe Walter can shoot it too and is quietly turning into a dependable heavy-minute wing.

With a win, Detroit could be in first or second in the East Group A division. The Orlando Magic (2-0) take on the struggling Brooklyn Nets (0-1) tonight. Should Orlando snag a win, they stay atop the group.

One game and one week at a time for Detroit in this tournament. They smacked around the Nets in their first cup game and look to do the same against the Raptors.

Projected starting lineup

Detroit Pistons (10-4): Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

Toronto Raptors (5-10): Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, Jamison Battle, Scottie Barnes, Jakob Poeltl

Question of the Day

The New York Knicks won the NBA Cup tourney and the real thing last year. Did that add any validity to the tournament?

lions.headline: Detroit Lions grades: Offense, defense, coaching all take blame in loss to Bears
lions.body:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell yells out onto the field during the first half of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

Let’s hand out some grades for the Detroit Lions’ 39-35 loss to the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.

Quarterback: A-

Jared Goff got off to a slow start against the Chicago Bears and missed on a couple of early throws. But, my goodness, he was absolutely on fire from the end of the second quarter on. In the second half alone, he was 12-of-14 to 120 yards and an interception that wasn’t really his fault. He was hitting on just about every kind of throw: deep posts, comebacks, crossers, seam shots. Goff was going toe-to-toe with Caleb Williams and, man, it was fun to watch until it wasn’t.

Running backs: A+

Jahmyr Gibbs may have wrapped up Offensive Player of the Year honors with his 252 scrimmage yard performance that also included three trips to the end zone.

Gibbs finished with 114 rushing yards over expected in this game—a single-game high for any running back this year—averaging +5.4 RYOE per rush (second-best among all RB games this year). I’ve run out of things to say about Gibbs. He’s electric, and we’re all lucky to be watching him on a weekly basis.

Tight ends: B

Sam LaPorta’s touchdown grab at the end of the first half was damn impressive and long overdue. He finished the game with four catches for 44 yards and that score. It was a quieter day from the other tight ends, but Detroit found some success in the run game with 12 personnel, so they deserve credit for doing some of the grunt work.

Wide receivers: B+

Amon-Ra St. Brown was torching the Bears’ secondary for most of the game, while also making some ridiculous contested catches. He posted a +22.7% catch rate over expected, his best output of the year. His seven catches for 146 yards were second-most he’s had this year and seventh most in his career.

The rest of the crew was relatively quiet, and Jameson Williams deserves at least part of the blame for the interception, even if it was tipped before it got to him. He did have a couple of deep routes that he beat the defender, including one Goff hit him for a 39-yard gain, but the interception proved too costly to ignore.

Offensive line: A-

If this were based just on play on the field, the offensive line may have earned an A+. The Bears registered just 13 pressures per PFF (for comparison’s sake, the Lions had 27), and the Lions were creating gaping holes in the run game. Jeffery Simmons was shockingly not much of a factor in this game, outside of some games he was playing.

Unfortunately, I have to drop this to an A-, because of the penalties. Forced or unforced, four false start penalties are unacceptable in a home game, and Christian Mahogany’s petty taunting penalty cost the Lions a valuable point.

Defensive line: B-

Derrick Moore and Alim McNeill were absolute game wreckers in the first half. The two combined for three sacks, and Moore’s two forced fumbles were the biggest reason Detroit had a two-score lead at halftime.

Unfortunately, the magic disappeared in the second half. Caleb Williams had plenty of time to go through his progressions in the second half, leading to 218 passing yards and two touchdowns in the second half alone.

Additionally, the Lions run defense took a massive step back. The Bears finished with 146 yards, three touchdowns, and a ridiculous 61% success rate running the football.

Linebackers: F

It was a brutal day from the linebackers, who consistently lost track of running backs and tight ends on play-action rollouts, or route combinations designed to create conflict. Here’s how PFF credited each linebacker in coverage:

Malcolm Rodriguez: 6 catches, 8 targets, 103 yards allowed (116.7 passer rating)
Trevor Nowaske: 1 catch, 1 target, 12 yards (116.7)
Derrick Barnes: 3 catches, 4 targets, 18 yards, 1 PBU (83.3)
K.J. Britt: 3 catches, 3 targets, 33 yards (112.5)

They, too, shared their blame in the run game woes.

Secondary: D

I thought it was another strong game from Roger McCreary, who tallied three passes defended and wasn’t credited with a single allowed catch. Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph made some strong plays in the run game, as well.

Unfortunately, the other two starters in the secondary—Rock Ya-Sin and Andre Cisco—were huge liabilities out there. Ya-Sin, who took full blame for the performance after the game, was credited with five catches allowed for 65 yards and both touchdowns. Cisco was more of an issue in the run game, getting caught out of position several times.

Special teams: C

Jake Bates wasn’t at his best, missing a long extra point and putting a few kickoffs into the end zone. Jack Fox was decent, but one of his punts landed several yards deep into the end zone. There was nothing noteworthy from the return or coverage teams, so just an average overall day.

Coaching: C+

There is so much going on with coaching that I’m going to break things down into sections:

Decisions I approved of:

Forgoing the late field goal to go for it — It seems counterintuitive, but in a lot of ways, being up three is better than six late in the game. Being up six means the offense will do everything they can to score a touchdown and win the game. Being up three means they will settle for a field goal, if necessary. On top of that, all analytical models were decisively in favor of the decision. And with the defense struggling and the offense rolling, I have zero problem with the decision. The play call was pretty good, too. You just have to credit T.J. Edwards for making a great open-field tackle on Gibbs.

Taking the safety — At the time, I wasn’t sure what I’d do. It’s a tough, unique decision to either take the ball at Chicago’s 10-yard line or take the safety and the ball. Ultimately, I think it was the right decision because if Detroit had taken the ball, they’d likely score 3 or 7. But there was plenty of time left for Chicago to eat into that lead, because they had all three timeouts. Taking the safety and the ball pretty much ensured you were going to be, at worst +2 at the end of the half, +9 at the best. It worked out optimally in Detroit’s favor.

Decisions I am indifferent about:

Throwing on second down — Many believed facing a second-and-8 late in the game, Detroit should have continued to run the ball, force the Bears to use their timeouts, and grind out a late win. I don’t mind prioritizing getting the first down over running clock, and the pass game was working pretty well. That said, the Lions were also moving the ball pretty damn well on the ground, and it’s hard to stomach not giving Gibbs an opportunity to put it away (although he got his opportunity on fourth down).

Timeout usage on defense — Many believe Campbell was being reckless with his timeout usage, giving the Bears enough time to make the game-winning score. Campbell justified his decision by saying he was hoping to have enough time to get the ball back. Ultimately, I think Campbell was damned if he did, damned if he didn’t. The fact of the matter is the Bears got the ball with 2:17 left and a timeout. They had plenty of time to score, and they would’ve adjusted their tempo no matter how Detroit used their timeouts.

Decisions I didn’t like:

Passing on third-and-1 — At the Bears’ 36-yard line up three points with 6:13 left, the Lions opted to run a play-action pass on third-and-1. It was intercepted. Detroit had gotten so good recently with these short-yardage runs, whether it was a Goff sneak or Sione Vaki run, but they got too cute here, and it was a huge mistake.

I still think there was more good than bad here, but there’s no doubt that coaching had an impact on this one.

lions.headline: What everyone said about Detroit Lions, Jeffery Simmons false start controversy
lions.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears smiles prior to an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The CBS broadcast for the Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears Thanksgiving Day classic jumped all over an interesting controversy involving back-to-back false starts from Lions center Juice Scruggs in the second quarter. The two penalties set the Lions behind the sticks, and they punted two plays later.

But when the broadcast came back from commercial, they showed a replay that appears to show Bears defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons yelling out something loud that immediately resulted in Scruggs’ false-start flinches.

Let’s break down the controversy by looking at the rulebook and hearing everyone’s perspective about the situation via comments after the game.

NFL rulebook on simulating snap counts

Simulating a snap count—or trying to disrupt the offensive line verbally—is an unsportsmanlike conduct infraction that carries a 15-yard penalty. Here is the exact wording of the rule, which you can find in Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, subarticle i:

There shall be no unsportsmanlike conduct. This applies to any act which is contrary to the
generally understood principles of sportsmanship. Such acts specifically include, among others:

(i) Using acts or words by the defensive team that are designed to disconcert an offensive team at the snap. An official must blow his whistle immediately to stop play.

So if Simmons was indeed yelling or screaming to intentionally get the Lions to jump, that should carry a 15-yard penalty in Detroit’s favor.

CBS announcer (and former DL) J.J. Watt

"It's a little defensive line trick. You normally can't ever get caught doing it because people can't see you."@JJWatt noticed something in the trenches 🔎 pic.twitter.com/6ECMxiHaY3
— NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 26, 2026

J.J. Watt was the one to point this out on the broadcast, calling it out as a penalty. But he also described why it’s so easy to get away with as a defensive lineman.

“He barks a little bit or he says something right here, and that’s when Scruggs moves. It’s a little defensive line trick. You normally can’t ever get caught doing it, because people can’t see you. But I think he is getting a little reason for Scruggs to be dropping back.”

Bears DL Jeffery Simmons

Simmons claims he was just calling a defensive alert to his teammate during those plays, and not trying to simulate the snap count.

“If I say, ‘Run,’ I’m telling my defense, run. Think I care to tell them what they about to do? I’m talking to my guys. So all the crying that they’re doing, that’s a them problem, not me.”

Lions guard Christian Mahogany

Mahogany was the most outspoken of the group, blatantly calling out Simmons for the infraction—while also admitting it’s still on the offensive line not to false start.

Via the Free Press:

“They’re simulating the snap count. They’re using − they find out the snap count of the quarterback and they use it, and that’s it. They use the words. So like I said, no bitching and complaining, we self-inflicted those wounds and we can’t false start.”

Lions coach Dan Campbell

Campbell clearly wasn’t in the mood to talk about the controversy, initially shutting down the first question he got about it. When pressed, he said he had an idea of why the false starts were happening. But when asked why, he shut it down again.

“No, I’m not going to share it. So, we’ll be good on that. We’ll be good. We’ve got to clean it all up and make sure that we just take care of our business. That’s all.“

Lions quarterback Jared Goff

Goff was far more direct, accusing Simmons of indeed simulating the snap count. However, the Lions quarterback downplayed the impact, noting it happened only once or twice and that the team needs to handle it better.

“I only think he did it really once that was really egregious to me – where they yell. It’s a really hard thing to officiate because at what point is he simulating the snap count? At what point is he just talking to his guys? And I understand it happens all across the league, this isn’t the first time it happened. But yeah, I’m just trying to make sure that they know that I’m not allowed to simulate snap count with my hands. He shouldn’t be allowed to do it with his voice. And that wasn’t the difference in the game. But yeah, that was early, and I don’t believe it happened more than once or twice.”

Later adding, “We got to be able to handle that a little bit better than we did.”

lions.headline: Discussion: Are you feeling better, worse about Detroit Lions after loss to Bears?
lions.body:
Nov 26, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) is tripped up by Detroit Lions defensive back Andre Cisco (28) and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (23) in the first quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

It’s never good to lose to a division rival. It’s even harder to swallow the loss when it feels like self-inflicted wounds turned a likely win into a painful loss.

That’s what Detroit Lions fans are going through this Black Friday, as they try to cope with the Lions blowing a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to lose a pivotal game to the Chicago Bears. But after the sting of the loss wears off, we’ll have to assess the team and what Thursday’s loss means for the season.

Maybe you’re still not over it. Maybe you’re still seething over certain plays or play calls. But for now, let’s assess where things are at. Today’s Question of the Day is:

Do you feel better, worse, or the same after the Lions’ loss to the Bears?

My answer: Thursday’s game confirmed a lot of good things I knew about the Lions. Their run game is back, their offensive line is playing their best football, and this team’s offense will keep them alive in just about any game. Jahmyr Gibbs is an insane weapon to have, and when Jared Goff is dealing, no one can stop them.

Remember that going into this game, the Bears were considered one of the best defenses in football. Detroit just hung 549 yards and 35 points on them—and it probably should have been even more. For three straight weeks now, the Lions have played decent-to-great defenses, and they’ve hung at least 30 on each. That has to make you feel pretty good right now.

Unfortunately, Thursday also presented the first real test of this defense in months, and they failed spectacularly. All of the problems that we saw earlier in the season—missed assignments, poor run defense, failure to capitalize on opportunities to get off the field—re-emerged. It begs the question as to whether all of Detroit’s defensive improvements over the past couple of months were real or the result of playing poor offenses.

Particularly concerning is the play of the linebacking corps, where Detroit doesn’t seem to know who they can depend upon. With Jack Campbell out, there is no one linebacker that is the defense’s rock. Derrick Barnes barely played in the first half, Malcolm Rodriguez was a huge liability for most of the day, K.J. Britt’s magic seems to have worn off, and even Trevor Nowaske struggled.

Additionally, while Derrick Moore had a fantastic first half, Detroit’s pass rush disappeared in the second. Aidan Hutchinson’s presence was certainly missed constantly in the final two quarters when the Lions defense just needed one more play.

The good news is that Detroit’s defense was also missing a few key pieces that they’ll likely get back soon. Defensive end DJ Wonnum and safety Chuck Clark would’ve made a difference in this game. Detroit’s nickel and dime looks with Clark, Brian Branch, and Kerby Joseph at safety could alleviate some of the linebacker issues. And Wonnum can help with pass rush.

So, ultimately, I feel a little worse. The defensive problems aren’t likely to completely go away soon. But with how the offense is playing right now, I still believe everything can be on the table for this team.

How are you feeling after the Lions’ 39-35 loss? Vote in the poll below and share your thoughts in the comment section.

lions.headline: 12 winners, 7 losers from Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears
lions.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

It was a Thanksgiving feast for offenses on this day. Unfortunately for the Detroit Lions, they were on the wrong side of a 39-35 barnburner.

The Chicago Bears pulled ahead with a last-second touchdown pass, the culmination of a defense that could not find its footing. The Lions got some phenomenal performances from the offense, including Jahmyr Gibbs going over the 200-yard mark, but it wound up not mattering as the defense could not force Chicago off the field.

This game was Detroit’s biggest test since Week 8, and while there were some positives, a lot has to go wrong to lose a game like this. Let us examine the winners and losers from this Thanksgiving Day tilt.

Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature.

Loser: Kelvin Sheppard, DC

The Lions defense had impressed over the last six games, but there was the caveat that they came against weak opponents. Detroit’s first game against Chicago would be their first true test—how could they handle a high-flying offense?

The answer: they couldn’t.

It was near-universal failure from the defense, specifically in the second half. The Bears turned two third quarter possessions into touchdowns. In the fourth quarter after the Lions scored a 70-yard touchdown to go up 35-24 with 8:20 left in the game—normally the dagger—the defense utterly collapsed. They gave up an uninspired, 71-yard touchdown drive in just one minute and three plays. Detroit was fortunate that the Bears had a turnover on downs on their next drive, but promptly allowed a 68-yard touchdown drive to end the game.

The Lions were constantly getting beat in the flats, allowing D’Andre Swift to rack up a team-leading 97 receiving yards. Caleb Williams rarely had to make difficult decisions or throws because the flat was consistently open to attack. It’s difficult to say initially if there was a schematic issue or a performance issue, but both problems reflect poorly on Sheppard. This persisted throughout the game—it’s one thing to get beat like this early, but to get beat drive after drive on the exact same play is beyond frustrating, it’s incompetent. Couple this with the Lions opting to rush just three players on the pivotal final Bears goal line possession, and it was defensive malpractice from Detroit.

Even if Detroit rebounds in the next weeks against the Atlanta Falcons or Tennessee Titans, how much faith are you actually putting in the defense? Detroit might not face another top-tier offense until their trip to Chicago in January, so my concerns about the performance of this defense will remain until then.

Winner: Derrick Moore, DE

No Aidan Hutchinson, no DJ Wonnum. Enter Derrick Moore. He was a game-changer early on Thanksgiving. In the first half, this was his stat line: four tackles, two sacks, and two forced fumbles, one of which resulted in a safety (and the ensuing drive ended with a touchdown). Chicago scored just 10 points in the first half and Moore’s performance was a key reason why.

Moore was held off the stat line in the second half, but there are some extenuating circumstances. For one, Chicago started to attack the flats more and more, thus giving the Lions pass rush little time to attack. Considering that the Bears were in obvious passing downs for most of the second half, the pass rush largely fell on him, rookie Anthony Lucas, or the blitz. Secondly, it was noted that Moore had a heating pad on his knee, showing he was battling some kind of injury. Also, on the Lions’ lone second-half sack by Malcolm Rodriguez, Moore was a hair behind him and would have had the sack otherwise.

All in all, you can see the difference Moore can make when things are clicking.

Winner: Jared Goff, QB

Goff was locked in on Thanksgiving. Last week against the Buccaneers, Goff had one of his best games of the year, and his encore performance this week was just as good. Play after play, Goff was making brilliant throws with pinpoint accuracy. He and Amon-Ra St. Brown had a telepathic-like connection—on multiple instances, Goff put the ball in the exact spot where St. Brown would be, even with a defender a hair out of place. Goff isn’t afraid to throw a block either. I don’t fault him for the interception, as it was tipped and bounced off the hands of Jameson Williams.

Goff finished the day going 25-of-36 for 313 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. I don’t fault him for the interception, as it was tipped and bounced off the hands of Jameson Williams. Goff is as steady as they come. He will never outrun defenses, nor is he an incredible scrambler, but he is smart and poised. Those are two traits that are invaluable for an NFL offense. I did not love the failed second-down pass to Brock Wright late in the game, both in terms of play call or execution—that one play was the extent my complaints with Goff on the day.

Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy are MVP frontrunners right now, but Goff should be on their heels. Although…

Winner: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB

…you can make a legitimate case that Gibbs is the MVP as well. Gibbs finally got his breakthrough run this week, scampering 70 yards down the field for his third score of the day. He finished the day with an absurd 205 rushing yards on 21 carries plus three touchdowns. He quietly added five catches for 47 yards as well. A performance like this would be a game-winner under normal circumstances, but the Lions defense wasted it.

Week in, week out, Gibbs is the spark plug of the offense. He is the rare non-quarterback worthy of earning the title of Most Valuable Player. Unfortunately, having Gibbs and Goff on the same team arguably works against them with regards to MVP voting—quarterback is the more valuable position, yet Gibbs is playing at such a high level. I would personally have Gibbs ahead in that race, but we shall see come award season.

Winner: Juice Scruggs, OC

This is a hot take, I know. Three false start penalties should normally get Scruggs into the loser category, but I think there is a valid excuse for at least two of them: Bears defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons was seemingly yelling the snap. This is illegal by the way, not some savvy veteran move. After the second false start, Simmons received a talking to by the officials during a commercial break. It is unclear if Simmons was again jawing to force Scruggs’ third false start, so I will dock him for that one at least.

Aside from the penalties, Scruggs was dynamite as a blocker. The CBS commentary crew wouldn’t mention it, but Simmons was getting worked by the Lions interior and Scruggs specifically. On the pivotal 39-yard catch by Jameson Williams at the end of the first half, it was Scruggs putting Simmons on the ground:

Goff to Jamo downfield for 39 yards!

CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uzCbjt86qP
— NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026

If you rewatch the game, I implore that you watch for Simmons’ orange sleeves. More often than not, it was Scruggs winning those battles, not the All-Pro defensive tackle. Simmons finished without a sack and per PFF’s live stats, just one pressure recorded. Considering that Scruggs had a tough time versus Vita Vea last week, seeing him succeed against Simmons like this is a massive win. Penalties can be cleaned up, especially when the other side should have been flagged for it instead.

Loser: Malcolm Rodriguez, LB

Normally one of the Lions’ most athletic cover linebackers, Rodriguez looked anything but on Thursday. In coverage, he looked incredibly sluggish. On a D’Andre Swift reception, his slow reaction led to him getting stiff-armed en route to a 33-yard reception. On the ensuing play, Rodriguez failed to stick with Stephen Carlson on a Caleb Williams bootleg, resulting in a catch to set up Chicago deep in Lions territory. In the fourth quarter, he got juked by Williams on a scramble, giving Chicago a close fourth down attempt that they wound up converting—if Rodriguez gets the tackle immediately, the Bears likely have to punt. He saved that drive with a third-down sack a few plays later, but it was a day with more bad than good.

Loser: Derrick Barnes, LB

I try to avoid listing a player as a “loser” if their role was insignificant, but I have to put Barnes in this category for that same reason: he was seemingly benched against the Bears. When Jack Campbell went down with injury, the expectation was that Barnes would lead the linebacking group. Only a few weeks later, he has tumbled down the depth chart. Rodriguez seeing an uptick of snaps was not unexpected, but Barnes getting out-snapped by Trevor Nowaske and K.J. Britt for most of the game is a shock. Barnes would get an expanded role in the second half, but partly because Rodriguez rolled his ankle.

Barnes had a touchdown-saving pass breakup late in the game, but it was otherwise a forgettable outing for him.

Winner: Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR

St. Brown has been playing second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs this season, but do not let that detract from his impact. St. Brown finished as the Lions’ leading receiver and he earned it with multiple tough catches. On one play, he got sandwiched by two defenders right after the catch, yet he still held on. On another, he dove out and landed hard on his shoulder and head. He stepped out for a bit but returned to action soon after.

Like Goff, he is a steady presence for the Lions offense. You know what you’re getting with him, and that is sure-handedness, elite route roughing, and toughness.

Quick hits:

Winner: Roger McCreary, CB
McCreary continues to play strong football after a rough early season. He logged three passes defended on Thursday, one of which was a tipped ball on a blitz.

Loser: Rock Ya-Sin, CB
Ya-Sin got beat for a pair of touchdowns, and while his coverage was generally fine, there were plenty of instances were you’d hope for a pass breakup rather than a tackle.

Winner: Sam LaPorta, TE
LaPorta got into the end zone for the first time since Week 5. After a slow stretch, he has now put together back-to-back solid performances.

Winner: Trevor Nowaske, LB
In general, it was a rough game for the linebackers, but Nowaske was the exception. He continues to impress when called upon, looking fast yet disciplined as a run defender and in coverage. He deserves to be an every-down player going forward.

Loser: Anthony Lucas, DE
It was a tough ask for the undrafted rookie, but he looked unrefined as a pass rusher and a liability in run defense. On multiple occasions, he failed to set the edge, resulting in a big Chicago play. Sprinkle in a taunting penalty, and it was not a great game.

Winner: Mehki Wingo, DT
Filling the role of Skyler Gill-Howard, Wingo had some great pass rushing reps, including nearly getting to Williams on the Moore strip-sack-safety.

Winners: Tyleik Williams and Alim McNeill, DTs
The Bears run game had zero success up the middle due to Williams and McNeill holding down the fort. McNeill also added a sack. They have quietly developed into a top-tier tackle duo in the league.

Loser: K.J. Britt, LB
Britt had some tough assignments against a good stable of Bears running backs, but he struggled keeping up at times. A bit of a return to earth for the former Patriots practice squader.

Winner and Loser: Christian Mahogany, OG
Mahogany was a snow plow on offense, bullying the Bears interior next to Penei Sewell and blasting lanes for Gibbs. However, the taunting penalty—even if it was a weak call—ultimately cost Detroit dearly. Being up 4 points instead of 3 changes the course of that final drive.

Loser: Jake Bates, K
Mahogany gets blamed for the taunting penalty, but Bates should still make a 48-yard kick. If he does, all of this discussion becomes moot.

lions.headline: 6 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving loss to Chicago Bears
lions.body:
Nov 26, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs the ball against Chicago Bears cornerback Clark Phillips III (20) in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Here are six takeaways after the Detroit Lions’ frustratingly blown game against the Chicago Bears.

Coaching decisions were critical, but not necessarily wrong

The tipping point of this game rested on a couple of big coaching decisions by Dan Campbell. On the Lions’ final drive of the game, Detroit got pretty aggressive, opting to prioritize moving the ball rather than bleeding clock. After a big Jahmyr Gibbs run got the Lions into field goal position with under three minutes left, Detroit opted to pass on second down, resulting in an incomplete pass and stopping the clock. Then, facing a fourth-and-4, Campbell opted to go for it rather than attempt a 51-yard field goal to potentially make it a six-point game. T.J. Edwards made a fantastic play to stop Gibbs short.

Analytics were generally in favor of the fourth down decision, and we’ve seen the Lions put the game away so many times on offense because of their aggression. Personally, I think it was the right decision, especially with the way the defense was flailing.

If there was a mistake on the coaching staff, I believe it was on the previous series. The Lions faced a third-and-1 in Bears territory, and opted to run a play-action pass that was ultimately intercepted. The Lions have been so good at third-and-shorts lately with the running game and/or a quarterback sneak, and I wish they would’ve kept on that. But at the same time, the Lions should have been able to convert there with the play call they had, but they didn’t execute.

And let’s not forget Campbell’s decision at the end of the first half to accept the penalty that resulted in a safety, erasing a fumble recovery. It was a controversial decision, but it netted the Lions nine total points—a big gain for Detroit.

You take the good and bad, but there were far more bigger issues that caused this loss, including…

Bad penalties

The Lions offense was disjointed early because of an odd string of false start penalties. Yes, maybe Jeffery Simmons was playing some games with the snap, but Juice Scruggs still has to stay disciplined.

The bigger issue is the taunting penalties. Christian Mahogany got tagged for one that moved an extra point back and was ultimately missed. That one point changed how both teams played the rest of the game. Anthony Lucas cost the Lions 15 critical yards of field position after they had just gotten a turnover on downs late in the game, as well. On the final defensive drive, D.J. Reed committed a critical 15-yard facemask penalty.

Nine penalties for 70 yards is too much, but these penalties particularly hurt because they came in critical moments.

Lions need linebacker help

Detroit has been doing a decent job keeping the boat afloat without captain Jack Campbell, but the damn broke on Thursday. Caleb Williams was constantly checking down to his running backs and tight ends, and the linebackers were nowhere to be seen in coverage. D’Andre Swift finished with seven catches for 97 yards, Sam Roush had five for 31, and it probably would’ve been even worse if Colston Loveland didn’t get injured earlier in the game.

Detroit also had their worst run defense game in quite some time, and a lot of times it felt the linebackers were out of position. Chicago managed 146 yards on 24 carries for 6.1 yards per carry and three touchdowns.

Jahmyr Gibbs is going to win Offensive Player of the Year

It sucks the Lions squandered such an incredible game for Jahmyr Gibbs, who rushed for 205 yards and three touchdowns on 21 carries. He was electric, and he finally broke out the explosive runs we’ve been waiting to see.

He has already surpassed last year’s rushing totals with 1,303 yards, his 5.4 yards per carry is currently the second-best in his career, and his 16 rushing touchdown ties a career-high—with six games remaining.

He’s going to be fun to watch for a long, long time.

Incredible, Jah pic.twitter.com/3qCDDVlqLB
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

Derrick Moore is ballin’

While he—and the entire Lions defense—disappeared a bit in the second half, Lions rookie Derrick Moore had a bigger impact on this game than anyone in the first half. He tallied two sacks—one strip-sack that resulted in a safety—plus a punch-out forced fumble that ended a threatening Bears drive. He was single-handedly carrying the defense in the first half, and he is off to a monster start to his career.

His 6.5 sacks on the season is second only to DJ Wonnum on the team, and he’s now tied for the team-lead in forced fumbles. Oh, and his name is now permanently etched with some NFL legends.

The only rookies in @NFL history to produce at least 6.5 sacks and 2 FFs in any four-game span:

1. @Lions EDGE Derrick Moore (2026)
2. Micah Parsons (2021)
3. Julius Peppers (2002)
4. Leslie O'Neal (1986)#OnePride pic.twitter.com/9UWu7fZSMz
— Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) November 26, 2026

Giddy up, the NFC North is going to be fun

For as frustrating as that game was, it was also pretty damn entertaining. The Lions and Bears showed they are very evenly matched, and while Chicago has the edge now, there is still plenty of football to be had. Detroit is just a game back of Chicago, and with a Week 17 matchup at Soldier Field, that can be made up in a literally one game.

Detroit is going to regroup after a tough 11-day stretch here, they’re going to win more games and make the playoffs. And everything remains in front of them despite this disappointing outcome.

lions.headline: Lions, Bears recap: Late-game blunders sink Detroit on Thanksgiving
lions.body:
Sep 13, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions fans make their wat to Ford Field prior to a game between New Orleans Saints and Detroit Lions fr the opening weekend of the NFL season. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

For most of the Thanksgiving Day game, the Detroit Lions were in control of the Chicago Bears. The Lions didn’t trail for the entire game… until the final three seconds.

Despite an outstanding effort on offense—putting up 35 points and over 500 yards of offense—the day will be remembered by a couple of opportunities in which they failed to put the game away. A late interception and an even later failed fourth-down conversion gave the Bears just enough space to mount a comeback, and that’s exactly what they did.

The Lions defense didn’t have a ton of answers for the Bears offense, as Caleb Williams threw for 345 yards and two touchdowns, while Chicago also added 146 yards and three touchdowns.

With the loss, the Lions drop to 8-3 on the season, and the Bears move to 9-2 at the top of the NFC North.

Here’s how the whole game shook out:

First quarter

The Lions won the toss and elected to take the ball first, in a change of normal strategy. Detroit’s offense got off to a strong start with a 6 and 7 yard run from Jahmyr Gibbs and a 19-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown.

Starting right guard Tate Ratledge exited the field with a limp and went straight to the blue tent. He was replaced by Miles Frazier. Ratledge was initially ruled questionable to return with an ankle and knee injury. He would return to the lineup after missing the next drive.

But the Lions kept driving, and St. Brown made a ridiculous one-handed, 27-yard catch to put the Lions first-and-goal from the 9-yard line.

Amon-Ra only needed one hand! pic.twitter.com/9JASlhQK13
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

However, the Lions stalled from there with back-to-back incomplete passes from Goff, and Detroit had to settle for a chip-shot field goal. 3-0 Lions.

The Bears quickly drove down the field, with Caleb Williams finding a few wide-open receivers, including D’Andre Swift for 13 yards and Kalif Raymond for 12. But when they moved into the red zone, Lions rookie defensive end Derrick Moore punched the ball out of Coleston Loveland’s hands and Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the fumble for a big turnover.

OUR BALL!

Derrick Moore punched it out, Malcolm Rodriguez recovered it! pic.twitter.com/Fznm4bMLb5
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

Detroit took over at their own 16, but quickly went three-and-out. A pitch to Gibbs was snuffed out by the Bears, turning a second-and-3 into a third-and-6. And Goff couldn’t find anyone open on third down, eventually throwing a ball off St. Brown’s fingertips for an incomplete pass.

But Detroit’s defense answered the call with a forced three-and-out of their own. A nice pressure from Anthony Lucas nearly forced an interception on second down, and Luther Burden was tackled well short of the sticks on third down by safety Andre Cisco, who was in for Chuck Clark.

On the drive, Bears tight end Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room.

Detroit’s passing attack hit another big play—a seam route to St. Brown for 23 yards. The All-Pro receiver took a big hit, but managed to hold onto the ball to put the Lions at their own 40-yard line.

Sheesh, Amon-Ra pic.twitter.com/ulmgDghxIl
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

A facemask penalty gave the Lions another 15 yards, and pushed them into Bears territory. Then a 14-yard catch from Gibbs and an 11-yard run by Jameson Williams moved the Lions into the red zone as the first quarter expired.

Second quarter

On a third-and-3 play, Gibbs ran up the gut for a 9-yard gain down to the Bears’ 1-yard line. Two plays later, Gibbs’ second effort pushed Detroit into the end zone for a 10-0 Lions lead early in the second quarter.

Happy ThanksGIBBSing pic.twitter.com/yycv1nrD0M
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

The Bears quickly answered with an explosive run. Salvon Ahmed broke off a 46-yard gain down the right sideline and into the red zone.

Salvon gets loose for 46 yards 💨

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/mqAbZN1MbH
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

But Detroit locked them down from there. Derrick Moore picked up a sack on first down.

Derrick Moore SACK 😤 pic.twitter.com/gxLRfenQP5
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

Then, on third-and-long, a blitzing Roger McCreary knocked down the pass at the line of scrimmage to hold the Bears to three. 10-3 Lions.

Detroit’s next drive was marred by back-to-back false starts from center Juice Scruggs. That forced a third-and-11, and Jared Goff, with all sorts of time, tried to check it down to Sione Vaki, but missed him.

Chicago took over on their own 20-yard line. Caleb Williams exploited a coverage bust on third-and-3, finding a wide open Stephen Carlson for and 18-yard gain. Then Swift caught a short pass, made a few Lions miss and took it for a big 33-yard gain.

D'Andre Swift down the sideline for 33

CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Evztsk1rWG
— NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026

A few plays later, Kyle Monangai ran it in for a 1-yard touchdown, tying the game up with 4:07 left in the half 10-10.

KYYYYYLE MONANGAIIIIII in the end zone again 🎶

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/ZILeJEydVn
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

The Lions got back to work with a 28-yard strike to St. Brown on the very first play of the drive. However, disaster nearly struck on the next play, with Goff tripping, fumbling, and jumping on his own recovery. The Bears challenged the call—thinking Goff never regained possession—but there was not enough evidence to overturn it.

Still, the 10-yard loss was enough to end Detroit’s drive. Goff missed Williams on a deep shot, and then he had to scramble on a third-and-20 and didn’t come close.

That gave the Bears a shot to run their two-minute drill to take the lead before half. But on the first play, Williams was sacked all the way back at his 2-yard line, setting up a second-and-18 at the two-minute warning. After a 7-yard gain on second down, Williams was strip-sacked and the Lions receovered. But there was an illegal batting penalty on the Bears, giving the Lions a choice:

Take the penalty, which results in a safety and possession

Decline the penalty and take the ball on the Bears’ 10-yard line

Detroit opted to take the safety points and the ball. 12-10 Lions.

ANOTHA ONE, D-MOORE pic.twitter.com/hEvpEOIXIl
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

Detroit was able to add more points on the ensuing possession. They overcame another pair of false starts thanks to a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak. Then Goff hit Williams on a bit 39-yard corner route into the red zone.

39 yards in the bucket for Jamo! pic.twitter.com/Ds7rd8QOsA
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

That gave the Lions eventually one shot at the end zone with 10 seconds left. Goff was able to hit Sam LaPorta up the seam for the score and a 19-10 Lions lead at halftime.

Jared Goff perfect ball placement to Sam LaPorta for a TD before the half!

CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RNd20GIm58
— NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026

Third quarter

The Bears chipped into the Lions’ lead to start the second half. Williams continued to attack the Lions’ linebacking corps with a 14-yard pass to Kyle Monangai. Then on third-and-6, Williams split Detroit’s deep zone with a 25-yard strike to Luther Burden all the way down to the Lions’ 25-yard line.

After a 5-yard scramble and an incomplete pass, the Bears faced a third-and-5. Williams found Ahmed for a 9-yard gain to the 11-yard line. Three plays later, Monangai bullied his way in for the touchdown. 19-17 Lions.

Thankful for @kylemonangai 🙌

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/pge3BG2Qdz
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

To make matters worse for the Lions defense, linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) and cornerback Roger McCreary (neck) suffered injuries on the drive. Both were listed as questionable to return, but both would later return to the lineup.

Goff continued to heat up with a couple of big throws—a 13-yarder to LaPorta, and a diving grab from St. Brown for 17. Then on third-and-9, Goff hit LaPorta on a post route for 17 yards, setting up a first-and-goal from the 8-yard line. A pass interference call on the Bears made it first-and-goal from the 1-yard line, and Gibbs walked in with ease to make it a two-score game again. 26-17 Lions.

Gibbs powers it in for his second of the day pic.twitter.com/P39yTcIe7v
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

The Bears continued to attack the Lions’ linebackers in coverage on the ensuing drive. Williams found Swift for 18 yards, then tight end Sam Roush for another 11. Then Swift took a draw play for a 30-yard touchdown—and the shootout was on. 26-24 Lions.

@DAndreSwift TO THE HOUSE

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/QhxRgV9qLN
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

The Lions looked to strike right back, and a 33-yard run from Gibbs—a patented reverse-field rush—put them right back into field goal position.

Incredible, Jah pic.twitter.com/3qCDDVlqLB
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

But a negative receiver screen to Williams set up a third-and-11, and Goff checked down to Williams well short of the sticks. That set up a Jake Bates 40-yard attempt to start the fourth quarter.

Fourth quarter

Bates drilled it to make it 29-24 Lions one play into the fourth quarter.

Detroit had an opportunity to get off the field after forcing a fourth-and-2, but the Bears went for it. And Williams found Rome Odunze in tight coverage for a 5-yard gain. But that’s all Chicago could manage. The Lions forced a third-and-10, and sent Malcolm Rodriguez on a blitz. He got home for the 10-yard sack, forcing a punt.

Rodrigo bringing the 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/NCsCMOT24c
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

The Lions avoided a three-and-out when Goff hit Jamo on a cross for a third-and-3 conversion. On the next play, Gibbs finally broke the big run, outrunning the entire Bears defense for a 70-yard touchdown.

and he's gooooooooooooooooooone pic.twitter.com/sjzJCK19A6
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

Christian Mahogany was called for taunting on the play, setting the extra point 15 yard back, and Bates missed it. 35-24 Lions.

With still over eight minutes to go, the game was far from over, and the Bears went to quick work on the Lions defense. It took them just three plays and one minute of game time to find the end zone with the drive ending in a 41-yard strike to Rome Odunze.

🗣️ ROOOOOOOME ODUUUUUNZE

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/UT288bDUIE
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

The Bears went for two and Caleb Williams carried it in for the conversion. 35-32 Lions.

Detroit wasn’t about to blink. On the first play of their drive, Goff found St. Brown for a 22-yard gain into Bears territory. But then a critically bad play happened that shifted the entire game. On a third-and-1, the Lions ran play-action and Goff tried to hit Williams, but the receiver couldn’t haul in the pass and it deflected off his hands for an interception.

LET'S GO, @DillonThieneman 😤

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/0DbfqyMsoB
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

Chicago couldn’t take advantage of the turnover, though. On fourth-and-2, Williams lofted a prayer deep, and it looked like Luther Burden had it, but Kerby Joseph wrestled it away for an incomplete pass, and the Lions took over on downs with 2:41 left.

WOW

The Bears were THIS close to a miraculous 4th down conversion 🤯

📺 CBS & Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/wjKZTKSJlH
— NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 26, 2026

Gibbs broke out another big run—a 34 yarder—but went out of bounds and stopped the clock, leaving a small crack for the Bears to still get the ball back.

Another 34 for Jahmyr puts him over 200 rushing yards today. pic.twitter.com/N4jRoCoGiY
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026

Detroit couldn’t move the ball after that, setting up a fourth-and-4 from the Bears’ 33-yard line with 2:22 left. The Lions opted to go for it, and Goff’s swing pass to Gibbs was stopped short.

Huge tackle by TJ Edwards to stop Gibbs and the Lions on 4th down!

CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kWFyGkhRGC
— NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026

That left 2:17 left on the clock for the Bears to score a field goal to tie, touchdown to win.

The Lions had an opportunity to put the game away on defense with a fourth-and-1 situation at the two-minute warning. But Williams on a QB keeper got the end for a 2-yard gain. Then he checked down to Odunze for 11 yards. Then the Lions got hit with a 15-yard facemask penalty that put the Bears in field goal position. Chicago faced a big third-and-5, and a toss to Swift picked up the first down.

A quick pass to Gibbs set the Bears up first-and-goal. With 12 seconds left, the Bears had two shots at the end zone to win it. Derrick Barnes knocked down the first attempt on a great play. But on the next play, Williams delivered the kill shot on a toe-tapper to Odunze. 39-35 Bears.

THAT'S A TOUCHDOWN!!!!!!

📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/IOUvYvWOHa
— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026

On Thanksgiving, people are surrounded by loved ones, enjoying food, and most importantly, watching Detroit Lions football. It’s a classic tradition across Michigan, but it doesn’t always end well, as the franchise has a losing record on the holiday. This time, though, they aim to make it a happy Thanksgiving with a win over the Chicago Bears, and what better way to do it than with some extra cash coming to you too!

It was another dominant week for me on the bets last week: I went 3-0 on all my straight bets, and if the refs hadn’t called some horrible defensive pass interference penalties on the final Lions defensive possession, it would’ve been a perfect day on the bets. We also hit our first bold bet parlay, so I can’t complain too much. Stay with me here as I try to keep the hot streak going, so make room on that plate for these bets.

Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook.

1. Over 55.5 Points (-112)

Hope you saved room for some offense because this game should have it. In their first battle last year, the Lions dominated the Bears 52-21 in Bears head coach Ben Johnson’s first game back in Detroit. Detroit won the season finale, but it wasn’t as explosive, 19-16. This year, I expect it to be more of a fight, and both offenses will be humming along.

Detroit enters at 28.8 points per game, while Chicago averages 26.2. Now the Lions defense has been playing better lately, holding their last four opponents to an average of 12.7 points per game, while the Bears defense started strong but has allowed an average of 22 points per game in their last four games. I expect Johnson will want revenge from 2025, and doing so on Thanksgiving will make it that much sweeter. This is the same coach who wants to lead the NFL in all-time scoring offense.

I think this game could be a high-scoring, close contest, with each team putting up at least 30 points. Each team has plenty of weapons, and as a divisional game, the stakes are higher. The winner takes control of the NFC North and, given how contested the division is, could determine how the standings fall come January.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.93

Since I could see this game being high-scoring, I think Lions quarterback Jared Goff will have a dominant performance against the Bears. The reason isn’t the Bears defense itself; it’s also how Goff has performed against them recently.

Last season, Goff threw for over 300 yards in both games: 334 yards and five touchdowns in their dominant Week 2 victory, and 331 yards in the low-scoring season finale. Despite the Bears’ defensive line upgrades, Detroit’s offensive line is a big improvement from 2025. If Goff can throw for over 300 with that line, how can he not do it again this year?

What also helps Goff this year is the Bears’ inconsistent pass defense. They’re either shutting down passing attacks, holding six teams to under 200 yards, or they’re letting them air it out, with three games where they’ve allowed over 300 yards. Goff has thrown for over 300 yards in four games so far this season, and if teams keep paying attention to running back Jahmyr Gibbs, Goff will gladly slice and dice them upfield.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $23.20

3. Amon-Ra St. Brown Over 82.5 yards (-113)

It wasn’t just Goff who went off on the Bears last season; wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had some strong performances. In the first game, St. Brown had six catches for 115 yards and three touchdowns, then snagged 11 balls for 139 yards in the last game. St. Brown made it a point to go off against his former coordinator in Johnson, and as long as he’s the head coach of the Bears, I think St. Brown will try his best to play well.

He’s averaging 84 yards a game this season, so I think hitting the over on this game is a must. Detroit lost its Thanksgiving game last year too, and I don’t think St. Brown wants Johnson to rain on the Detroit parade. He will do whatever it takes for Detroit to win this game, and with the offense humming, I wouldn’t put it past St. Brown to have another great performance this week.

Speaking of St. Brown, you best believe he will want to find the end zone on Thanksgiving. If he doesn’t get as many yards as he wants, but scores at least once and comes away with the win, I think he would be content with his performance. While this game isn’t as big as the Germany game, St. Brown wants to play well when matched up against Johnson.

With my expectations of this game being high-scoring, I see the passing offense taking the stage against the Bears. If Goff is throwing for over 300 yards, I think he throws three touchdowns as well. He’s done it three times this season, but he hasn’t done it at home in Ford Field. That changes when Goff put up a big performance on Thanksgiving afternoon.

So far, I’ve hyped up Goff and St. Brown, but I don’t think I’ll overlook Jameson Williams for a good performance too. While his play has been up and down this season, I think he’ll find the end zone and gobble up some turkey on Thursday afternoon. Goff could throw three touchdowns to St. Brown as they did against the Bears last year, but I think he spreads the wealth and gives Williams one, perhaps on a unique trick play that catches Johnson’s defense by surprise.

michigan.headline: Michigan Football players explain what beating Ohio State means, even in a down season
michigan.body:
Michigan safety Rod Moore Jr. (1) walks onto the field for Senior Day celebration ahead of kickoff between Michigan and UCLA at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

Ahead of The Game between Michigan and Ohio State, the Wolverines’ players had some thoughts of their own to share with the media earlier this week.

“I’m going back home,” defensive back and Ohio native Rod Moore said. “I’m maybe finishing my Michigan career back at home, and so I think it’s very important to me, especially because it’s probably not the most even matchup, but we both have our share of losses, our share of defeats this year, and it’s kind of gonna be probably the most gritty — grittiest one I’ve been a part of, to be honest.”

“I would say there’s nothing like it, honestly,” tight end Jalen Hoffman said. “It’s kind of weird. It’s hard to describe because there’s nothing you can really describe it or make that is similar like it.”

“Yeah, it’s definitely there,” linebacker Troy Bowles said, referring to losing last year’s matchup. “I’m trying not to think about it obviously, but I mean, it’s there and the game’s coming at the end of the season. So I feel like it’s fuel to play harder and to wanna be at your best when this game rolls around at the end of the year.”

“I mean, it’s Michigan-Ohio State, right?” offensive lineman Evan Link said. “It’s pride, it’s the history of this game, it’s living up to everything that’s gone before, right? I mean, I’ve grown up around this rivalry my whole life and it’s so special, right? If you can win this game, that’s something you can forever hold your head on, that no matter what else happened that season, you’d beat Ohio State. And that’s something you can always feel good about.”

“Yeah, I think for anyone who thinks it really doesn’t feel the same, I think you kind of missed the point,” defensive lineman Trey Pierce said. “The Game, it always usually has implications, but I think these two teams, we just have so much history that that’s what really informs the game and what makes it so special, what makes it so big. Yeah, the implications aren’t as big this year, but it’s still the biggest game of the year for both teams. Like, you have a bad season, you beat Ohio State.”

The Wolverines take on the Buckeyes this Saturday in Columbus at noon.
